audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentions Goes Where He Pleases. Mundo's passive resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, costing him health and dropping a chemical canister he can walk over to heal and shorten the passive's cooldown.
audit.why: This is the single most important interaction in the matchup for a champion whose entire plan is 'W-root into Q'. The first Twisted Advance root does not land — it gets eaten. The follow-up plan has to be: bait the passive, then root, and deny or contest the canister so the trade isn't refunded.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and mid now state the passive, the canister and the bait-then-root order.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mundo's Q is called 'Infected Cleaver' in six fields — that is the old name; it is Infected Bonesaw. spikes[2] also says the poke 'pays his Q mana' when every Mundo ability costs 0 mana (it costs health). Maokai's W is repeatedly called a 'W-pull' when Twisted Advance is a dash to the target.
audit.why: Wrong ability name, invented resource cost, and a mis-described own-ability.
audit.corrected: Names fixed across whys[2], spikes[0], spikes[2], early, mid, late, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0]; the mana claim removed; 'W-pull' replaced with the dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Mundo levels 6 and first item and called 3 and 4-5 'Skill', while whys[4] on the same page says the level-6 window is Maokai's and the packet chart and the published Mundo-side audit both read Maokai through first item.
audit.why: Four rows disagreed with the mirror and with their own why text.
audit.corrected: Rows 2,3,4,5 flipped to Maokai in both layers with ratings raised to match the mirror's 3/4/4/4/4/4/7 from the other side; row 6 stays Dr. Mundo.

audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4s and free, Heart Zapper 17s at rank 1, Maximum Dosage 120s. Rank-1 numbers are what the player sees while the lane is being decided.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Goes Where He Pleases: eats your FIRST root and drops a canister — contest the pickup or the trade refunds itself. - Heart Zapper: 17s, the burst is his heal. - Infected Bonesaw: 4s and free. - Maximum Dosage: 120s.

edits.before: Track Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. When it is down — W-Q + R him.
edits.after: His passive eats your first root and drops a canister — deny the pickup or the root bought nothing.

edits.before: Your W-pull into Q knockback with Sap Magic healing beats a single-ability Mundo before his Q cleaver and heals come online.
edits.after: Your W-dash root into Q knockback with Sap Magic healing beats a single-ability Mundo before Infected Bonesaw and his heals matter.

edits.before: You out-trade him repeating W-Q, but his Infected Cleaver percent-HP poke starts healing him back, so the edge narrows to a skill window.
edits.after: You out-trade him repeating W-Q, and Infected Bonesaw's 4s poke charges your Sap Magic as fast as it chips, so level 3 still belongs to you.

edits.before: You keep winning short root trades, but his Q heals let him stay in lane, so neither of you can fully take the stage.
edits.after: You keep winning short root trades and his Bonesaw only keeps him in lane — he cannot punish your step-up through 4-5.

edits.before: Your Bami/Sunfire spike keeps you lane-stable and even, but his cleaver heals back the chip, so it comes down to who plays the trade cleaner.
edits.after: Your Bami/Sunfire spike out-paces his regen while Grievous Wounds is up, so the first-item window is still yours to force trades in.

edits.before: W-pull into Q knockback with Sap Magic healing lets you bully a single-ability Mundo before his Q cleaver and passive heals come online.
edits.after: W-dash root into Q knockback with Sap Magic healing bullies a single-ability Mundo before Infected Bonesaw and his regen come online.

edits.before: Bami/Sunfire line keeps you even and lane-stable, but his cleaver percent-HP poke starts paying his Q mana and heals back into the trade.
edits.after: Bami/Sunfire keeps you lane-stable, and since Infected Bonesaw costs him no mana at all, bring Grievous Wounds before you convert the chip.

edits.before: Mundo is one of the weakest level-1s in the game and so are you, but you spike first: at 2-3 your W-pull into Q knockback plus Sap Magic healing wins every short trade before his Q cleaver and passive heals are online. Dodge or body-block his Infected Cleaver (Q) — it's percent-HP poke that also heals him, so eating it for free pays his whole lane. Step up on his Q cooldown, W-pull, Q-knock, and walk away healthier than him.
edits.after: Mundo is one of the weakest level-1s in the game and so are you, but you spike first: at 2-3 your W-dash root into Q knockback plus Sap Magic healing wins every short trade before his regen matters. Body-block Infected Bonesaw (Q) — it is a 4s percent-HP poke and free to cast, so eating it pays his whole lane. Step up as it flies past, W in, Q-knock, and walk away healthier than him.

edits.before: Through levels 4-6 you keep repeating the W-Q trade and your saplings (E) deny his cleaver last-hits and zone him off the wave. At 6 your R doesn't give you a kill — Mundo's heals are too strong for that — but it's an enormous gank-setup tool, so root him and let your jungler collapse rather than trying to solo him. The truth: you can chunk him all day, but you cannot finish a Mundo who plays around his Q heals, so convert lane pressure into roams and tempo instead.
edits.after: Through 4-6 you repeat the W-Q trade while saplings deny his Bonesaw last-hits. Know the order, though: Goes Where He Pleases resists your FIRST immobilise and drops a canister, so the opening root is bait — make him spend it, stand on the canister, then root for real. At 6 your R won't kill him through his heals but it is an enormous gank-setup tool, so root and let your jungler collapse rather than soloing a drain tank.

edits.before: This is where it slips. Once Mundo has 2+ items his Maximum Dosage (R) heal and percent-HP Q cleaver make him genuinely unkillable in a 1v1, and your tank damage was never going to keep pace. Stop trying to win the lane and start winning the map — your R, saplings, and W lockdown turn every skirmish and objective fight your way. Don't get caught splitpushing into a drain tank who out-sustains you; group, root, and let your carries do the killing.
edits.after: This is where it slips. Once Mundo has 2+ items his Maximum Dosage heal and the percent-HP Bonesaw make him genuinely unkillable 1v1, and your tank damage was never going to keep pace. Stop trying to win the lane and start winning the map — your R, saplings and W lockdown turn every skirmish and objective fight your way. Don't get caught splitpushing into a drain tank who out-sustains you; group, root, and let your carries kill.
